The ASV realizes this one written verb twice, restarting the clause for the second object with the italic *oppressed they*; both realizations are its one discontinuous unit (rules 34, 25), headed on the first. The competing reading marks *oppressed they* `added` under rule 20, but the Hebrew does write this verb, which rule 34 makes decisive.

review_notes: The italic *oppressed they* is read as the second realization of the written רָצַץ rather than as supplied English, since the Hebrew writes that verb in this same clause (rule 34); the italics corroborate nothing either way (rule 7).
*that year* carries no written preposition, so the בְּ is unrepresented while the demonstrative takes the phrase's single determiner (rules 40, 41).
